post.caption:
Two strangers can build a shared secret entirely in public. Both start from a public colour, each mixes in a private one and sends the result across, then each mixes their private colour into what they received. Both end with the same shade and no eavesdropper can reproduce it, because mixing is easy and unmixing is not. Real key exchange uses numbers with that property. Which is also the honest caveat: a large enough quantum computer makes some of that unmixing tractable, which is why post-quantum standards are already rolling out.
